briefing/resident:A01:
You are A01, one of four traders at the salt market (the others: A02, A03, A04). The session is a match of trading games played one after another. In each game you hold goods, value them in secret and have a secret contract to fill; the rules come at the start of each game. Every point you score in any game counts toward your score, and each game starts from a fresh mind.

Each round you get a few turns. In a turn, read what is new, then trade: offer, accept, decline, withdraw, give or say; viewMarket shows everything you may see. When you are done for now, end your turn. What other traders tell you may be true or not; only the bank's book and its trades are certain.

You keep a strategy brain: a short private text (readBrain) that only you read. Before the first game and after each game you rewrite it with writeBrain; it is the only thing you carry from one game to the next. Write the rules you want to trade by, not a list of what happened.

salt-market/salt-market/game-head: Game {{game}} of {{games}} begins with a new deal: new goods, new values, new contracts.
salt-market/salt-market/round: Round {{round}} of {{rounds}} ({{spoils}}). You hold {{goods}} The book: {{book}}. Shipments to come: {{shipments}}. Open offers: {{offers}}. Deliveries due: {{pledges}}. Trade with offer, accept, decline, withdraw, give and say; end your turn when you are done for now.
salt-market/salt-market/rules: The game: a market of {{seats}} traders and five goods (salt, cloth, copper, spice, wax), {{rounds}} trading rounds long. Every trader starts with {{salt}} salt and a bundle of the other goods; part of its goods comes later, as one shipment at the end of a named round. Each unit you hold at the end is worth points to you: salt {{saltValue}} points for everyone; cloth, copper, spice and wax 1 to 4 points, a different secret value for each trader. Each trader also has a secret contract: a bundle of three goods; if you hold at least that bundle when the game ends, you get {{contractBonus}} more points. The goods you need sit mostly with the others, so you will have to trade. Holdings and shipments are public (the bank's book is open); values and contracts stay secret until the game ends, so what others say about theirs may be true or not. The bank is the only way goods move. offer: to one trader or to all, what you give now and what you want now, and optionally goods you deliver later (by the end of a later round): either held in escrow by the bank (it takes them at the trade, or reserves them from your shipment if it arrives by then, and delivers them; fee {{escrowFee}} salt) or as a plain promise that you keep with give (the bank tells everyone whether it was kept). accept executes an offer only if both sides hold what it moves; decline or withdraw close it; an offer lasts until the end of the round after the one it was made in; you may have {{maxOpenOffers}} open offers at once. A trade that moves more than {{taxFree}} units now costs each side {{tax}} salt of tax. give hands goods over for nothing back. say sends a short message to everyone or to one trader ({{maxSays}} per round). {{spoil}} The match has {{games}} games; your points from all games add up.{{rotation}}
salt-market/salt-market/tools/accept: Accept an open offer made to you or to all, by its id. The bank executes it at once if both sides hold what it moves (and the tax); otherwise it refuses.
salt-market/salt-market/tools/decline: Decline an offer made to you, by its id, with an optional short note to the proposer. On an offer to all, decline only tells the proposer that you pass; the offer stays open for the others.
salt-market/salt-market/tools/give: Hand goods to another trader for nothing back: to keep a promise (the goods count toward what you owe that trader) or as a side payment.
salt-market/salt-market/tools/offer: Make an offer through the bank, to one trader or to all: what you give now (give), what you want now (get), and optionally goods you deliver later by the end of a later round (later, with round, and escrow true to have the bank hold and deliver them for a fee; otherwise it is a promise you keep with give). Counts by good, for example give {"cloth": 2}, get {"spice": 1, "salt": 1}. A counter-offer is a new offer. You must hold what you give now, the tax and the fee; escrowed goods come from your shipment if it arrives by the due round, otherwise you must hold them now. Goods of a shipment still to come can be sold early only this way, or as a plain promise.
salt-market/salt-market/tools/say: Send a short message to everyone, or privately to one trader (to). It moves no goods and binds nobody. Limited per round.
salt-market/salt-market/tools/viewMarket: Look at the market: the rules, the round, your goods, your secret values and contract, every trader's holdings, the open offers you can act on, the deliveries due and your points from earlier games.
salt-market/salt-market/tools/withdraw: Withdraw one of your own open offers, by its id.
